record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: If n and m are distinct positive integers, are Th(F_n) and Th(F_m) distinct?

evidence.quote: 1.18∗ . (A. M. W. Glass [11], Problem 41) If n and m are distinct positive integers, are T h(Fn ) and T h(Fm ) distinct?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) is a group $(G,\cdot,{}^{-1},e)$ equipped with a lattice order $(\wedge,\vee)$ such that the group multiplication distributes over the lattice operations on both sides; i.e., $a(b\wedge c)d=(abd)\wedge(acd)$ and $a(b\vee c)d=(abd)\vee(acd)$ for all $a,b,c,d\in G$. The variety of ℓ-groups is considered in the first-order language $\mathcal{L}=\{\cdot,{}^{-1},e,\wedge,\vee\}$. For each positive integer $n$, let $F_n$ denote the free lattice-ordered group on $n$ generators (the free object on $n$ generators in the variety of ℓ-groups), and let $\mathrm{Th}(F_n)$ denote its complete first-order theory in $\mathcal{L}$.

Question: If $n$ and $m$ are distinct positive integers, must the theories $\mathrm{Th}(F_n)$ and $\mathrm{Th}(F_m)$ be distinct? Equivalently, are the free ℓ-groups $F_n$ and $F_m$ elementarily inequivalent whenever $n\neq m$?
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous question for free abelian ℓ-groups has been answered affirmatively (Glass–Macintyre–Point: free abelian ℓ-groups of distinct ranks greater than 2 are not elementarily equivalent). For the non-abelian free ℓ-groups $F_n$ in the variety of all ℓ-groups, no published resolution was located in the search; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Free abelian lattice-ordered groups (ScienceDirect)
status_evidence.snippet: Finitely generated free abelian ℓ-groups with distinct ranks are not elementarily equivalent (Glass, Macintyre, Point).
status_evidence.claim: The abelian analog of the question is solved affirmatively; the non-abelian case for free ℓ-groups is not addressed there.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups (arXiv:0906.2621)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 1.18*: If n and m are distinct positive integers, are Th(F_n) and Th(F_m) distinct?
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an unsolved problem in a compilation of open problems on ordered and lattice-ordered groups.
